extracted.intended_audience: cartoonists, comic artists, and humor writers interested in process and single-panel/diagrammatic humor
extracted.subtask_description: Process notes and a working rubric for creating cartoons that use diagrams, labels, and interior-life material to produce recognition-based humor. Focuses on form choice, image-vs-caption balance, frequency of practice, and the source of the laugh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of diagrammatic form (diagram/label/list) to enable subversion
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the cartoon use a form (diagram, label, list) the joke can violate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finck's signature is the DIAGRAM as joke form: a labeled image where the labels reveal an emotional truth the diagram pretends to neutrally describe. Diagrams promise objectivity; filling them with subjective, emotional content violates the form — that violation is the joke. Choose a formal structure whose apparent neutrality you can undercut.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image carries majority of meaning (caption as label, not punchline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the image carry most of the meaning?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Finck, the image carries ~80% of the meaning; the caption (when present) functions as a label rather than the punchline. This inverts traditions where the caption is the punchline. Anti-pattern: relying on the caption to do the heavy comedic lifting while the image merely sets up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joke centers on an interior experience the reader will recognize
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the joke about an interior experience the reader will recognize?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finck's work normalizes neurotic interior monologue; universalizing the inside-of-the-head experience is the comedic move. The reader laughs at recognition — seeing their private thought made visible. Prioritize specificity of interior detail that leads to broad recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice frequency and lack of preciousness
rubrics_metrics.description: Have you produced enough recently to be unprecious?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finck publishes near-daily on Instagram; constant production prevents preciousness and lets the audience watch the comedic mind in motion. The rubric favors regular output and iteration rather than treating each piece as precious. Anti-pattern: over-polishing a single cartoon at the expense of voice and momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose the right format: single-panel vs. multi-panel
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the format (single, multi-panel) right for the joke?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single panel: maximum compression, requires a 'perfect lock' — ideal for interior-life comedy that needs clarity. Multi-panel: allows escalation and development but risks losing the viewer's eye and diluting compressed interior jokes. Select the format that preserves the joke's essential focus (clarity vs. escalation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Laugh should come from recognition ('I thought I was alone')
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the laugh come from 'I thought I was alone'?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the emotional payoff is the reader recognizing themselves in the presented interior experience. The desired comic effect is not cleverness alone but the comforting/shocking recognition of shared private behavior or thought. If the laugh doesn't rest on that recognition, reconsider subject or framing.
